lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The file includes a date of birth and nationality, personal details readers are not meant to weigh.
items.because: They are unrelated to assessing the résumé and take space from relevant content.

items.says: The dates leave an eight-month gap between the B.A. and the Operations Analyst role.
Education appears before Experience.
The business-case and roadmap outcome comes after the research methods and loss estimate.
items.because: It is harder to spot quickly.

items.says: The opt-in comparison does not establish that the redesign caused an outcome.
items.because: Merchants who opted in may differ from those who stayed on the old flow, so the comparison cannot isolate the redesign’s effect.

items.says: The comparison method has no stated outcome.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether onboarding improved or what the measurement found.

items.says: The 11%-to-7% figures are an adjusted rate, not evidence that actual late deliveries fell.
items.because: Excluding weather-delayed shipments changes which deliveries count; it does not show that fewer were late.

items.says: The method and training details after the result can be compressed.
The S&OP activities are listed without saying what they enabled.
items.because: The line does not show why the work mattered or what decision it supported.

items.says: “Prepares” is present tense in an entry for a role that ended in August 2023.
items.because: The tense conflicts with the dates and can make the timing of the work unclear.

items.says: The 1,800-hour figure is not identified as measured savings or a projection.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether it represents realized or forecast savings.

items.says: The route-planning rollout result is not the opening bullet in the entry.
The launch line does not say what product or rollout work you personally owned.
items.because: A reader can see the app’s reach but not the product-lead contribution behind it.

items.says: “Surplus-food” and “that would have been thrown away” repeat the same idea.
The weekly-active-user result comes after the interview context.
“Each week” and “a week” repeat the same timeframe.
The scheduling line describes meetings without stating a resulting change.
items.because: Without a concrete scheduling outcome, it does not show what the practicum achieved or why the work mattered.

items.says: The line does not say how much the form was shortened or what effect the change had.
items.because: Adoption shows the change was put into practice, but readers cannot judge its size or value.

items.says: The intake result is buried after the methods instead of leading the entry.
Passive voice hides who mapped the intake and shortened the form.
The merchant-onboarding result is assigned to the hospital practicum, where it does not belong.
items.because: It repeats the Harbor Payments result for the same 2,300 merchants under an unrelated project that ended before the internship began.

items.says: The bullet does not specify which part of onboarding was redesigned.
items.because: “Redesigning onboarding” does not tell readers what changed or let them assess the contribution.

items.says: “The time it takes” is wordy and present tense for a past result.
items.because: The practicum ended in May 2024, and the wording takes more space than a concise measure.
